overview.name: Polypropylene (PP)
overview.description: A versatile thermoplastic polymer known for its excellent chemical resistance, high melting point, and wide range of applications.
overview.overviewDescription: Polypropylene represents one of the most versatile and widely used thermoplastics, offering an exceptional combination of properties that make it suitable for applications ranging from food packaging to automotive components. This semi-crystalline polymer, derived from propylene monomer, provides excellent chemical resistance, high heat resistance, and superior mechanical properties compared to many other plastics. PP's unique balance of stiffness, toughness, and processability has made it indispensable in modern manufacturing, enabling the production of lightweight, durable, and cost-effective products.
keyFeatures: Excellent chemical resistance and heat stability
overview.industrialSignificance: PP is the second most important polymer globally, with annual production exceeding 80 million tons. Its versatility, performance characteristics, and cost-effectiveness make it essential for packaging, automotive, textile, and medical industries.

handling: Avoid excessive heat and direct sunlight

hazards: May release fumes at high temperatures
